issues.legal_issue: A repeat application for release of a building is not barred merely because it is made within the interval specified for giving effect to findings in an earlier application.
material_facts: An earlier application seeking permission to sue for eviction on the ground of personal requirement was rejected on its merits.
A later application sought release on the same ground and was made within six months of the commencement of the later rent statute.
issues.conclusion: The relevant rule does not bar the later application; it provides for the treatment of findings in the earlier proceedings, rather than requiring dismissal of the later application.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 18(1), made with reference to Sections 38(4) and 41, creates a rule of presumption intended to avoid multiplicity of proceedings; it does not impose a filing bar. The direction that the prescribed authority “shall” accept earlier findings is directory and, in context, means that the authority “may” accept them. The Court relied on the distinction between presumptions of law and presumptions of fact described in Phipson on Evidence; it cited no earlier cases.

rule.if: release_application_after_prior_permission_application and prior_application_decided_on_merits and repeat_application_on_same_ground and repeat_application_within_rule_interval

predicates.release_application_after_prior_permissi: A landlord makes an application seeking release after having earlier sought permission to bring an eviction action against the tenant.
predicates.prior_application_decided_on_merits: The earlier application was finally decided on its merits.
predicates.repeat_application_on_same_ground: The later application seeks release on the same ground as the earlier application.
predicates.repeat_application_within_rule_interval: The later application is made within the relevant interval following the earlier decision or the commencement of the new governing regime.

issues.definition: When a landlord makes a timely repeat release application on the same ground after an earlier merits decision, the timing alone does not bar the later application.

issues.legal_issue: Earlier findings need not control a repeat release application when material changes in circumstances have made those findings irrelevant.
material_facts: After the earlier application was rejected, the landlord could no longer live with his brother and had to live in a single room in another person's house.
An inspection found acute lack of space and significant discomfort in the landlord's accommodation.
About five years passed between the rejection of the earlier application and the later application.
The landlord sought release of the whole building or, alternatively, a part of it.
issues.conclusion: The changed living circumstances made the earlier findings irrelevant, so the presumption in favour of those findings did not apply to the later application; the grant of partial release was not erroneous.
issues.legal_principle: Under Rule 18(1), the prescribed authority may rely on findings in an earlier application when the circumstances remain unchanged and those findings remain relevant. The rule is a directory guideline, not an inflexible command to disregard material changes in circumstances. The Court referred to Rule 18(1), Sections 38(4) and 41, and the purpose of avoiding multiplicity of proceedings.

rule.if: release_application_after_prior_permission_application and prior_application_decided_on_merits and repeat_application_on_same_ground and material_change_in_landlord_circumstances and earlier_findings_no_longer_relevant

predicates.release_application_after_prior_permissi: A landlord makes an application seeking release after having earlier sought permission to bring an eviction action against the tenant.
predicates.prior_application_decided_on_merits: The earlier application was finally decided on its merits.
predicates.repeat_application_on_same_ground: The later application seeks release on the same ground as the earlier application.
predicates.material_change_in_landlord_circumstance: The landlord's circumstances materially change after the earlier application is decided.
predicates.earlier_findings_no_longer_relevant: The changed circumstances make the findings in the earlier proceedings irrelevant to the later application.

issues.definition: When a landlord makes a repeat release application and material changes make the earlier findings irrelevant, those findings need not control the new application.

issues.legal_issue: A court may order eviction from a specified part of a building under a single tenancy, even if the order leaves another part with the tenant.
material_facts: The tenant occupied the first and second floors as a residence and used the ground floor for a drug store belonging to his wife.
The landlord sought possession of the entire building or, alternatively, part of it.
The appellate authority allowed release of the ground floor alone.
issues.conclusion: The partial-release order was permissible; the Act allows eviction from a specified part of a building under tenancy.
issues.legal_principle: Section 21(1) of the U.P. Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act 1972 authorizes an eviction order from the building under tenancy or any specified part of it. The Court therefore rejected the contention that a single tenancy could not be divided into separate occupied portions for this purpose.

predicates.landlord_release_proceeding: A landlord seeks recovery of possession from a tenant in a release proceeding.
predicates.tenancy_covers_building: The tenant's tenancy covers the building from which possession is sought.
predicates.release_sought_for_specified_part: The landlord seeks release of a specified part rather than only the entire building.

issues.definition: In a landlord's release proceeding concerning a building under one tenancy, seeking release of a specified part permits eviction from that part.

issues.legal_issue: A comparative-hardship finding favouring the landlord is not erroneous where the tenant uses the portion to be released only for business and has alternative premises for that business.
material_facts: The tenant did not live on the ground floor and used it only for his wife's drug store.
The tenant had been given an adjacent building for the drug store business and could conveniently move the business there.
The landlord needed accommodation and would be more affected if possession were not ordered.
issues.conclusion: The appellate authority did not err in finding that the landlord would suffer greater hardship if possession were not ordered than the tenant would suffer from partial eviction.
issues.legal_principle: The comparative-hardship assessment was supported by the tenant's non-residential use of the ground floor and the availability of alternative premises for the business. The Court found no error in the appellate authority's assessment on those facts.

rule.if: appeal_from_partial_release_order and landlord_needs_accommodation and tenant_uses_released_part_only_for_business and tenant_has_alternative_business_premises

predicates.appeal_from_partial_release_order: The matter is an appeal concerning an order releasing only part of the tenanted premises.
predicates.landlord_needs_accommodation: The landlord needs the premises for accommodation.
predicates.tenant_uses_released_part_only_for_busin: The tenant uses the portion ordered to be released only for business and not as a residence.
predicates.tenant_has_alternative_business_premises: The tenant has other premises to which the business can conveniently be moved.

issues.definition: On an appeal from a partial-release order, a finding that the landlord faces greater hardship is not erroneous when the landlord needs accommodation and the tenant can move the business from the released part to alternative premises.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant whose remaining residential floors depend on facilities in the portion released may seek directions to secure access to those facilities.
material_facts: The tenant argued that the first and second floors could not be used as a residence without access to the bathroom and toilet on the ground floor.
The order released the ground floor while leaving the upper floors with the tenant.
issues.conclusion: The tenant may apply to the prescribed authority for directions requiring suitable provision for access to and use of the bathroom and toilet.
issues.legal_principle: The Court did not treat the location of the bathroom and toilet as invalidating the partial-release order; it identified an application for directions to the prescribed authority as the means to address access. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited for this disposition.

predicates.partial_release_order: An order releases part of a tenanted building while leaving another part with the tenant.
predicates.tenant_retains_residential_floors: The tenant retains floors used as a residence after the partial-release order.
predicates.necessary_facilities_are_in_released_par: Facilities needed to use the retained residential floors are located in the portion released.

issues.definition: When a tenant retains residential floors but necessary facilities are in the released portion, the tenant may seek directions for access to those facilities.
